Oil change and new air filter at Dunmore Garage in March, 48,200 miles. The mechanic said the front brake pads have about 3 mm left.

Next MOT is due in February. The rear wiper blade squeaks and should be replaced before then.

Maya and Leo start swimming lessons at the leisure centre on Saturdays at 9:30. Leo is in stage two, Maya in stage four.

[3] Car insurance renewal (https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/18c2f0a)
The car insurance with Harbourline expires on 14 November. The renewal quote came in at 612 pounds, up from 540 last year, mostly because of the new postcode band.
Comparison sites show two cheaper options with the same excess and windscreen cover. Ask Harbourline to match before switching; they matched last year after one phone call.
Remember to add the no-claims certificate and the dashcam discount code when filling in the new application.

[4] Moving to a new password manager (file:///home/sam/notes/tech/passwords.md)
Exported the vault from the old password manager and imported it into the new one. 412 logins came across; passkeys had to be recreated.
Turn on two-factor authentication for the new account, print the recovery kit and store it with the important documents.
Delete the export file securely once the import has been checked.

[5] Film night list (file:///home/sam/notes/social/films.md)
Films to watch: a Studio Ghibli classic for the children, the new documentary about deep sea exploration, and a noir double bill.
Popcorn maker is in the garage. Friday evenings work best.

[6] Fixing the bike (file:///home/sam/notes/misc/bike.md)
The rear derailleur on the bike skips gears. Replaced the gear cable and adjusted the limit screws; still slipping on the smallest cog.
The bike shop says the chain is stretched and the cassette is worn. New chain and cassette quoted at 85 pounds.

[7] Choosing a new laptop (file:///home/sam/notes/tech/laptop.md)
Shortlist for the new laptop: a 14 inch model with 32 GB RAM for running local models, or a lighter 13 inch with 16 GB and better battery life.
Must have: two USB-C ports, a good keyboard, Linux support. Budget up to 1,800 pounds. Wait for the November sales before buying.

[8] Parents evening booking - autumn (https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/19d40a2)
School booking system: the initial slot for Maya's autumn parents evening with Ms Okafor is Thursday 5 November at 17:40, ten minutes, in the Year 5 classroom.
Things to raise: how she is settling into the new class, whether she joined the debate club, and if the times tables practice is paying off.
Leo's slot still needs booking before the system closes.

[9] Monthly household budget (file:///home/sam/notes/finance/budget.md)
Household budget. Fixed costs each month: mortgage 1,120, council tax 168, energy 142, broadband 32, phones 28, insurance 61.
Groceries average 520 a month; eating out crept up to 190 in the summer. Target is 120.

[10] Year 5 trip to the Science Museum (https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/19d9c08)
Year 5 will visit the Science Museum in London on Friday 20 November to support our forces and space topic. The coach leaves school at 8:15 and returns by 4:30.
The cost is 18 pounds per child, payable on ParentPay, and the signed consent form must be returned by 9 November. Children need a packed lunch in a disposable bag and should wear school uniform.
Kind regards, Mrs Patel, Year 5 Leader

context.text:
[1] Q4 team objectives (file:///home/sam/notes/work/okrs.md)
Objective two: finish the Kestrel migration and decommission the MySQL cluster by December.
Objective three: reduce on-call pages by 30 percent by fixing the top five noisy alerts.

[2] Home insurance policy (file:///home/sam/notes/home-insurance.md)
Buildings and contents insurance is with Clearwater Mutual, renewing on 2 March. Accidental damage cover was added this year.

Bikes are covered away from home up to 800 pounds each.

[3] Power flush quote for the heating (file:///home/sam/notes/power-flush.md)
Following the engineer's advice after the boiler breakdown, asked Hearthside Heating to quote for a power flush of the central heating.
Initial estimate: 420 pounds for eleven radiators, including fitting a magnetic filter. Proposed date 6 November.

[4] Kestrel migration standup notes (file:///home/sam/notes/work/kestrel-standup.md)

The shadow reader found mismatches in currency rounding for refunds. Lena is fixing the decimal precision in the Postgres schema.
Cutover is still planned for the second week of September if mismatches stay low.

[5] Boiler breakdown and repair (file:///home/sam/notes/boiler.md)
The boiler stopped firing on Sunday night; the display showed fault code F28, which means ignition failure. No hot water or radiators until the engineer came.

The engineer recommended a power flush next autumn because the radiators upstairs are cold at the top.

[6] Self assessment tax return (file:///home/sam/notes/finance/tax.md)
The self assessment for the last tax year is due online by 31 January. Rental income from the flat and the freelance invoices both need to go on it.
Deductible expenses: letting agent fees, the boiler service at the flat, and a share of the home office broadband.
Pay the balancing payment and the first payment on account together. Keep receipts for five years.

[7] Swimming lessons for the children (file:///home/sam/notes/family/swimming.md)
Maya and Leo start swimming lessons at the leisure centre on Saturdays at 9:30. Leo is in stage two, Maya in stage four.
Bring goggles and a swim hat. The term costs 96 pounds each, paid by direct debit.

[8] Fixing the bike (file:///home/sam/notes/misc/bike.md)
The rear derailleur on the bike skips gears. Replaced the gear cable and adjusted the limit screws; still slipping on the smallest cog.
The bike shop says the chain is stretched and the cassette is worn. New chain and cassette quoted at 85 pounds.

[9] Roof leak in the spare bedroom (file:///home/sam/notes/roof.md)
Water stain spreading on the spare bedroom ceiling after the storm. The drip only appears during heavy rain from the west.
The roofer found two slipped slates and cracked flashing around the chimney. He replaced the slates and resealed the flashing for 380 pounds.

[10] Blood test results (file:///home/sam/notes/health/blood-test.md)
The annual blood test came back mostly normal. Cholesterol is 5.4, slightly above the target, and vitamin D was low at the end of winter.
The doctor suggested a vitamin D supplement from October to March and another cholesterol check in six months. Less cheese, more oats.

[1] Kestrel migration standup notes (file:///home/sam/notes/work/kestrel-standup.md)
Kestrel standup: the backfill of historical orders to Postgres is 70 percent done. Dual writes have been on for three days with no errors.
The shadow reader found mismatches in currency rounding for refunds. Lena is fixing the decimal precision in the Postgres schema.
Cutover is still planned for the second week of September if mismatches stay low.

[2] On-call runbook (file:///home/sam/notes/work/oncall.md)
When paged, acknowledge within five minutes and post in the incident channel. Severity one means customer-facing impact.
For gateway errors, check the connection pool dashboard and the last config deploy first. Roll back the deploy if it is less than an hour old.
Hand over open incidents at the Monday rotation with a written summary.

[3] Kestrel cutover rollback plan (file:///home/sam/notes/work/kestrel-rollback.md)
If error rates rise after the cutover, flip the reads flag back to MySQL first; dual writes keep MySQL current so no data is lost.
If dual writes themselves fail, stop the writer, replay the outbox from the last checkpoint, and reconcile with the nightly diff job.

[4] Project Kestrel: Postgres migration plan (file:///home/sam/notes/work/kestrel-plan.md)
Kestrel moves the orders service from MySQL to Postgres 16. Phase one runs dual writes behind a feature flag while a backfill copies historical orders.
Phase two switches reads to Postgres for 5 percent of traffic, comparing results with the shadow reader. Phase three cuts over fully once mismatches stay below 0.01 percent for a week.
Owners: Sam for the backfill, Lena for the shadow reader, Omar for the cutover runbook.

[5] Kitchen renovation quotes (file:///home/sam/notes/kitchen.md)
Three builders quoted for the kitchen renovation. Oakline estimate 18,500 pounds including worktops; Brightwell estimate 16,900 without appliances.
Brightwell can start in April and expects four weeks of work. Oakline is booked until June but includes the electrical certificate.
Decide on quartz versus laminate worktops before asking for revised estimates. The island needs two extra sockets.

[6] Cornwall holiday budget (draft) (file:///home/sam/notes/travel/cornwall-budget.md)
Draft budget for the Cornwall week in August. Rough figures only until we book.
Cottage near St Ives for seven nights: estimate 1,450 pounds. Fuel and parking about 180. Food and eating out 450. Surf lessons for the children 120. Days out, including the Eden Project, 100.
Draft total 2,300 pounds. The holiday pot should cover it by July if we keep moving 300 a month into it.
Still to decide: take Biscuit with us or book kennels.

[7] Power flush booked - revised quote (https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/19d5e31)
Booked and confirmed for Thursday 12 November, arriving at 8am. Clear access to the boiler cupboard and every radiator the night before.
Payment on completion by bank transfer. Bleed the radiators afterwards and check the pressure gauge is back to 1.5 bar.

[8] Blood test results (file:///home/sam/notes/health/blood-test.md)
The annual blood test came back mostly normal. Cholesterol is 5.4, slightly above the target, and vitamin D was low at the end of winter.
The doctor suggested a vitamin D supplement from October to March and another cholesterol check in six months. Less cheese, more oats.

[9] Q4 team objectives (file:///home/sam/notes/work/okrs.md)
Objective two: finish the Kestrel migration and decommission the MySQL cluster by December.
Objective three: reduce on-call pages by 30 percent by fixing the top five noisy alerts.

[10] Design review: search ranking (file:///home/sam/notes/work/search-review.md)
Proposal: replace the keyword-only search with hybrid ranking that fuses bm25 with embedding similarity using reciprocal rank fusion.
Open questions from the review: how to evaluate offline, whether to diversify results, and the latency budget for embedding the query.
Decision: build a labelled evaluation set first and report recall at ten before switching the default.

Holding a std Mutex guard across an await point makes the future not Send and can deadlock under a multi-threaded runtime. Use tokio's Mutex or drop the guard first.

Cancellation drops the future at its next await point, so cleanup must not rely on code after an await running.

context.text:
[1] On-call runbook (file:///home/sam/notes/work/oncall.md)
When paged, acknowledge within five minutes and post in the incident channel. Severity one means customer-facing impact.
For gateway errors, check the connection pool dashboard and the last config deploy first. Roll back the deploy if it is less than an hour old.
Hand over open incidents at the Monday rotation with a written summary.

[2] Flat rent review 2026 confirmed (https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/19e1f20)

Update the rental income spreadsheet and check the first payment arrives at the new amount.

[3] Notes on async Rust (file:///home/sam/notes/tech/async-rust.md)
Holding a std Mutex guard across an await point makes the future not Send and can deadlock under a multi-threaded runtime. Use tokio's Mutex or drop the guard first.
spawn_blocking is for CPU-heavy or blocking work such as synchronous SQLite calls; it runs on a separate thread pool.
Cancellation drops the future at its next await point, so cleanup must not rely on code after an await running.

[4] Postmortem: API outage on 3 June (file:///home/sam/notes/work/postmortem-june.md)
The public API was down for 47 minutes on 3 June. A config deploy set the connection pool size to zero on all gateway nodes.

[1] Project Kestrel: Postgres migration plan (file:///home/sam/notes/work/kestrel-plan.md)
Kestrel moves the orders service from MySQL to Postgres 16. Phase one runs dual writes behind a feature flag while a backfill copies historical orders.
Phase two switches reads to Postgres for 5 percent of traffic, comparing results with the shadow reader. Phase three cuts over fully once mismatches stay below 0.01 percent for a week.
Owners: Sam for the backfill, Lena for the shadow reader, Omar for the cutover runbook.

[2] Parents evening booking - autumn (https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/19d40a2)
School booking system: the initial slot for Maya's autumn parents evening with Ms Okafor is Thursday 5 November at 17:40, ten minutes, in the Year 5 classroom.
Things to raise: how she is settling into the new class, whether she joined the debate club, and if the times tables practice is paying off.
Leo's slot still needs booking before the system closes.

[3] Q4 team objectives (file:///home/sam/notes/work/okrs.md)
Objective one: make search feel instant. Key results: p95 search latency under 150 ms and zero timeouts on the mobile app.
Objective two: finish the Kestrel migration and decommission the MySQL cluster by December.
Objective three: reduce on-call pages by 30 percent by fixing the top five noisy alerts.

[4] Tom and Ellie's wedding (https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox/18d1e07)
RSVP to Tom and Ellie's wedding by 1 August. The ceremony is at 2pm in Ludlow on 19 September, reception at the barn afterwards.
Book the hotel in Ludlow for two nights; the gift list is at the department store online. Dress code is summer formal.

[5] Kestrel migration standup notes (file:///home/sam/notes/work/kestrel-standup.md)
Kestrel standup: the backfill of historical orders to Postgres is 70 percent done. Dual writes have been on for three days with no errors.
The shadow reader found mismatches in currency rounding for refunds. Lena is fixing the decimal precision in the Postgres schema.
Cutover is still planned for the second week of September if mismatches stay low.

[6] Flat rent review 2025 (file:///home/sam/notes/finance/flat-rent-2025.md)
The tenant, Mr Doyle, has been reliable and always pays on time, so a modest rise feels fair rather than pushing to the top of the range.
The agent's fee for the renewal paperwork is 60 pounds. Reply to Hartley Lettings by the end of September.

[7] Book club notes (file:///home/sam/notes/social/book-club.md)
This month's book club pick was a novel about a lighthouse keeper. Most people liked the first half more than the ending.
Next month we are reading a history of the printing press. Meeting at Grace's flat on the 14th at 7pm.

[8] Hiring a backend engineer (file:///home/sam/notes/work/hiring.md)
We are hiring a senior backend engineer for the payments team. The interview loop is a phone screen, a systems design session and a pairing exercise.
Three candidates are in the pipeline. Ana's take-home was the strongest; schedule her onsite before the end of the month.
Recruiter contact is Joe at Talentbridge; the agency fee is 18 percent of first-year salary.

[9] Power flush quote for the heating (file:///home/sam/notes/power-flush.md)
Following the engineer's advice after the boiler breakdown, asked Hearthside Heating to quote for a power flush of the central heating.
Initial estimate: 420 pounds for eleven radiators, including fitting a magnetic filter. Proposed date 6 November.

[10] Remortgage options (file:///home/sam/notes/finance/mortgage.md)
The fixed rate on the mortgage ends in May. The lender's product transfer offers 4.6 percent for five years with no fee.
A broker found 4.3 percent with a 999 pound arrangement fee at another bank. Over five years the broker deal saves roughly 1,400 pounds after fees.
